children: Mexico's 12-month inflation rate accelerated more than expected in the first half of September, while core inflation continued to ease, data from national statistics agency INEGI showed on Thursday.
Annual inflation in Latin America's second-largest economy hit 3.42% in the period, INEGI said, up from 3.26% a month earlier.
Economists in a Reuters poll had forecast it to come in at 3.37%.
Meanwhile, the closely watched core price index, which strips out some volatile food and energy prices, continued its downward trend.
Core inflation reached 3.79% in the 12 months through early September, down from 3.93% in the first half of August and slightly below economists' expectations of 3.81%.
Annual core inflation is within the Bank of Mexico's target range of 3%, plus or minus one percentage point.
On a monthly basis, consumer prices rose 0.33% during the first half of September, while the core price index was up 0.17%, INEGI said.
